pdf_note: J-STAGE open access scan (1 bit, 400 dpi); figures are part of the page scan

x_axis.note: left and right frame lines carry the labels 0 and 25 deg (no tick marks inside the frame; dotted grid lines at 5 deg steps agree, 38.2 px per deg)

y_axis.note: bottom and top frame lines carry the labels 0 and 1 (dotted grid lines at 0.2 steps agree, 672.5 px per unit)

marker.identification: manual: marker shape identified by eye on a 3 times zoom of the scan (open triangle in the legend); centre taken as the centre of the marker body bounding box, ignoring error bar caps

meta.source_title: Traveling performance evaluation of wheeled rover climbing various soil slopes (Sutoh, Nagatani, Yoshida; Proceedings of the 2012 JSME Conference on Robotics and Mechatronics, 1A2-L06, in Japanese)
meta.vehicle: two wheeled test rover, mass ballasted to 4.0 kg for every wheel set, axle distance 400 mm, wheel speed 2.50 rpm
meta.grousers: 3 lugs, 5 mm high; wheel surface covered with sandpaper of the soil grain size
meta.soil: Toyoura sand (JIS R 5200), cohesionless, nearly uniform grain size
meta.preparation: sand box 1.5 m long, 0.30 m wide, 0.20 m deep, tilted by hand; slope 0 to 24 deg in 4 deg steps; 3 runs per condition
meta.comparability_note: Slip ratio from the rover travel distance after the motion became steady, with the effective radius set by the lug geometry (Eqs. 1 to 5). Points are plotted values of 3 runs (error bars not transcribed; whether the marker is a mean is not stated in the text read). x is the nominal slope. The scan is 1 bit and markers of the six wheels overlap heavily at 0 and 4 deg and at 20 and 24 deg, so only markers whose shape and outline were clear were read; left out here: 16 deg marker hidden under the lugless filled circle; 0, 4, 20, 24 deg overlap. load_per_wheel_N derived here as 4.0 kg times 9.81 divided by 2 wheels, assuming even load. Cohesion 0 Pa (Table 1). Toyoura sand is a uniform fine quartz sand close to dune sand; the narrow 0.30 m bed may add side wall effects.
